recent_posts.title: AI Chatbot Safety Guardrails for Mental Health
recent_posts.summary: Researchers and clinicians are pushing for mandatory safety guardrails on AI chatbots used for companionship and mental health support, following links between AI relationships and psychological harm including suicides. Yale neuroscientist Ziv Ben-Zion proposes four safeguards: clear AI disclosure, detection of distress language, strict conversational boundaries, and independent clinical audits. Technical approaches include SHIELD and EmoAgent, LLM-based supervisory systems that monitor for risky language patterns. Sycophancy driven by RLHF training is identified as a key risk factor, as is 'drift' in prolonged conversations. Regulatory responses include the EU AI Act, U.S. state laws in New York, California, and Washington, and draft rules in China. A preprint study found Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.5 to be the safest mainstream chatbot in handling delusional content.

recent_posts.title: Familiar Machines and Magic reveals a quadruped social home robot to reinforce healthy routines
recent_posts.summary: Colin Angle, co-founder of iRobot, has unveiled the first robot from his new startup Familiar Machines & Magic (FM&M). Named 'Familiar,' it is a quadruped social home robot with 23 degrees of freedom, a touch-sensitive coat, vision system, microphone array, and an onboard edge AI stack using a custom small multimodal model. Unlike previous social robots that failed due to lack of long-term engagement, Familiar is designed to learn your routines and actively encourage healthier habits — like reducing screen time or prompting outdoor walks. It deliberately avoids speech, instead communicating through physical expressions like tail movement, ear wiggles, and facial cues. All AI processing runs on-device with no cloud data streaming. Pricing is compared to pet ownership costs (~$65–$100/month) but no commercial launch date has been set. FM&M sees this as a platform that could eventually specialize into elder care and parental support.

recent_posts.title: Managed Misalignment Rethinks AI Alignment Limits
recent_posts.summary: NetFreedom Pioneers' Toosheh system delivers curated data bundles over free-to-air satellite TV signals, bypassing Iran's internet shutdowns. By piggybacking data on MPEG transport streams, it reaches users with standard satellite dishes and no subscription. During Iran's 2026 protests and internet blackout, Toosheh distributed news, first-aid guides, anticensorship tools, and Starlink setup instructions to millions. The system is one-way and untraceable, making it resistant to typical blocking methods, though vulnerable to terrestrial jamming — countered with RAID-style redundancy. Operating costs run tens of thousands of dollars monthly, currently sustained by private donors after U.S. State Department funding ended in 2025. NFP is also developing intelligent content curation, local Wi-Fi redistribution, and educational deployments for Afghanistan.

recent_posts.title: MNW Deepfake Detector Tracks Evolving AI Artifacts
recent_posts.summary: Researchers from Microsoft, Northwestern University, and Witness have released the MNW deepfake detection benchmark, a diverse dataset of AI-generated images, audio, and video designed to help developers build more robust detection systems. Current detectors struggle in real-world settings because they are trained on narrow datasets from few generators and fail to generalize. The MNW dataset addresses this by drawing from many generators and including post-processed media that mimics real-world manipulation. It will be updated biannually each spring and fall to track evolving AI artifacts and evasion techniques, aiming to close the gap between lab performance and real-world detection accuracy.

recent_posts.title: Videos: Humanoid Robot Production, Mars Rovers, More
recent_posts.summary: IEEE Spectrum's weekly Video Friday roundup covers the latest in robotics, with a focus on humanoid robot production scaling. Figure is now producing 55 robots per week, while 1X has opened a 58,000 sq ft NEO Factory in Hayward, California for full-scale humanoid production with consumer shipments planned for 2026. Other highlights include Agility Robotics' Digit balancing on one leg, a tactile-enabled whole-body humanoid manipulation system, Boston Dynamics' Stretch robot perception Q&A, NASA's two Mars rovers exploring different eras of Martian history, Neuralink's surgical robot for implant procedures, and a look at Chinese-made Unitree G1 humanoid robots entering the US market via companies like OpenAI and Nvidia.

recent_posts.title: How Chip Speedups Transform Real-Time EPR Spectroscopy
recent_posts.summary: Researchers at CEA-Leti, University of Stuttgart, and USC are shrinking electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy systems onto chips, enabling portable, real-time detection of free radicals in beer, batteries, blood, and more. CEA-Leti's new chip uses injection-locked phase detection to sweep frequencies in just 200 nanoseconds — three times faster than competing systems — without a speed-limiting feedback loop, enabling detection of micromolar free radical concentrations in 10-nanoliter samples. Meanwhile, pulse-mode EPR chips (which expose samples to a band of frequencies simultaneously) are advancing at USC and Stuttgart, with Stuttgart's Jens Anders launching a startup called SpinMagIC to commercialize the technology, starting with food quality testing and eventually targeting cancer detection.

recent_posts.title: Taming Data Center Power Fluctuation With AI UPS
recent_posts.summary: Brain-computer interface (BCI) trial participants share their experiences with experimental neural implants from companies like Neuralink, Synchron, and Blackrock Neurotech. Users describe both the emotional and practical benefits — from playing video games to restoring speech and independent living — alongside challenges like neural drift, time-limited trials, and device durability. The piece explores the push to commercialize BCIs, newer wireless and less invasive designs, and debates around consumer applications, data privacy, and insurance coverage. Trial participants emphasize that agency and freedom of expression are often the most meaningful outcomes, even as the technology remains far from mainstream.
